                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inflammation of the patellar tendon
opb. Noninflammatory degeneration of the joint
opc. Infection of the joint
opd. Deposition of crystals in the joint
ope. Inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of right knee swelling, erythema, and fluctuance over the inferior patella, along with tenderness on palpation and limited range of flexion due to pain, are most consistent with prepatellar bursitis. This condition involves inflammation of the periarticular fluid-filled sac, which aligns with the consensus that bursitis can cause localized swelling and pain without systemic infection signs or joint line tenderness. The retrieved evidence paths support this by linking bursitis to pain and inflammation, confirming the diagnosis. Other options, such as joint infection, crystal deposition, or noninflammatory degeneration, are less likely due to the absence of systemic symptoms, joint line tenderness, or a history of trauma. Therefore, the most likely underlying cause of the patient's symptoms is inflammation of the periarticular fluid-filled sac, consistent with bursitis.
